Surah 73: Al-Muzzammil [Meccan except verse 20, which is Medinan; it has twenty verses]

﴿O you who are wrapped up (in garments)﴾ the Prophet. Its origin is al-Mutazammil; the taa' was assimilated into the zaay, meaning: the one wrapped up in his garments at the time the revelation came to him, out of fear of it because of its awesomeness.

Qur'an 73:2 reads: ﴿Stand [in prayer] through the night﴾

Commentary: Stand (pray) the night.
﴿Half of it﴾ is a substitute (badal) for ﴿a little﴾, and its being little is in relation to the whole. ﴿Or reduce from it﴾ from the half ﴿a little﴾, down to a third.

Or add to it, up to two-thirds (of the night); "or" here is for choice. "And recite the Qur'an" (warattil al-Qur'an) slowly and distinctly, pausing carefully in its recitation (tatharraf, from tarttil, meaning to recite with deliberate care).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 5:

﴿Indeed, We are going to send down upon you a speech﴾ — the Qur'an — ﴿heavy﴾ — awe-inspiring, or difficult, because of the obligations it contains.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 6:

﴿Indeed, the rising at night﴾ (qiyam, standing in prayer, after sleep) ﴿is more effective in tread﴾ (muwafaqat al-sam‘ li-l-qalb, the hearing being in agreement with the heart in comprehending the Qur'an) ﴿and more upright in speech﴾ (abyan qawlan, clearer in utterance).

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 7:

﴿Indeed, for you in the day is extensive occupation﴾ (tasarruf, i.e. being free to move about and busy yourself) in your affairs, in which you have no free time for reciting the Qur'an.

**Tafsir al-Jalalayn** (the commentary of al-Mahalli and al-Suyuti) on Surah 73, verse 8:

﴿And mention the name of your Lord﴾, i.e., say: "In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful" at the beginning of your recitation. ﴿And devote yourself to Him with complete devotion﴾, i.e., sever yourself (unto Him), ﴿with complete devotion﴾: the verbal noun of *batala* (tabtil, "devotion"), brought in for the sake of the rhyme (*fawasil*, the rhyming endings of verses), and it entails *tabattul* (devotion/detachment).
He is ﴿the Lord of the East and the West; there is no god but Him, so take Him as a trustee﴾ (wakil), [one] to whom you entrust your affairs.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 10:

﴿Be patient over what they say﴾, i.e., the disbelievers of Makkah, regarding their harm, ﴿and abandon them with graceful abandonment﴾, without impatience (jaza') in it; and this was before the command to fight them.

Translation of the passage from Tafsir al-Jalalayn on Surah al-Muzzammil (73), verse 11:

﴿And leave Me with the deniers﴾ (wa-dharnī): "leave me" (utruknī). ﴿And the deniers﴾ (wal-mukadhdhibīn) is in the accusative either as a conjunction with the object (of the verb "leave") or as an object accompanying it (maf'ūl maʿahu). The meaning is: I am sufficient for you against them, and they are the chieftains of Quraysh. ﴿Possessors of luxury﴾ (ulī al-niʿmah): plenty and ease (al-tanaʿʿum). ﴿And give them respite a little﴾ (wa-mahhilhum qalīlan): for a little time. So they were killed a short while after that at Badr.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 12:

﴿Indeed, with Us are shackles﴾ fetters, heavy ones; the plural of nikl, with the nun pronounced with a kasra. ﴿and a blazing fire﴾ a fire that burns.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 13:

﴿And a food that chokes⦆ that sticks in the throat, and it is al-Zaqqum, or al-Dari' (ḍarīʿ), or al-Ghislin (ghislīn), or a thorn of Fire that neither comes out nor goes down. ﴿And a painful punishment﴾ painful, in addition to what has been mentioned, for those who denied the Prophet (ﷺ).

On the Day the earth and the mountains will quake (تُزَلْزَل, be violently shaken), and the mountains will become a heap of sand (كَثِيبًا, rama), gathered together, flowing (مَهِيلًا), sand that pours out after being gathered. It is from هالَ يَهِيل (hala yahīlu, to pour or flow), and its original form was مَهْيُول. The damma upon the ya' was felt to be heavy, so it was transferred to the ha', and the waw was deleted as the second of the two unvocalized letters, since it was an added letter. The damma was then changed to a kasra to harmonize with the ya'.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 15:

﴿Indeed, We have sent to you﴾ O people of Makkah, ﴿a messenger﴾ who is Muhammad (ﷺ), ﴿as a witness against you﴾ on the Day of Resurrection, concerning what proceeds from you of disobedience, ﴿just as We sent to Pharaoh a messenger﴾ who is Musa (upon him be peace).
Pharaoh disobeyed the Messenger, so We seized him with a heavy seizing. (Wabīlan) severe.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 17:

﴿So how will you guard yourselves, if you disbelieve,﴾ in the world, ﴿on a Day﴾ which is the object of ﴿guard yourselves﴾, i.e., its punishment. ﴿By what fortress will you fortify yourselves against the punishment of a Day﴾ ﴿that will make the children grey-haired﴾, plural of ashyab (grey-haired), because of its terror, and it is the Day of Resurrection. The original vowel of the shin in shiban is a damma, but it was given a kasra to harmonize with the yā' (of the following word). It is also said that for an intensely terrible day one says "a day that greys the foreheads of children," and this is a metaphor, though it is permissible that the intended meaning in the verse is the literal one.

﴿The sky will be split asunder by it﴾, meaning that it is cleaving (inshiqaq), by that Day because of its intensity. ﴿His promise﴾, may He be exalted, concerning the coming of that ﴿is ever fulfilled﴾, meaning that it is certainly going to happen, without doubt.
Indeed, this (the frightening verses) is a reminder (تَذْكِرَة, an admonition) to the creation. ﴿So whoever wills takes a path to his Lord﴾, that is, a way to Him through faith and obedience.

Commentary of al-Mahalli & al-Suyuti (Tafsir al-Jalalayn) on surah 73, verse 20:

﴿Indeed, your Lord knows that you stand [in prayer] less than two-thirds of the night, or half of it, or a third of it﴾ (aqall, "less"), ﴿and a group of those with you [also does so]﴾. The reading bi-l-jarr (in the genitive) makes "thuluthay" (two-thirds) the object of a conjunction, i.e., "[less than] two-thirds, half, and a third," and bi-l-nasb (in the accusative) makes it governed by adna (less). Their standing [in prayer] is likewise, similar to what He commanded at the beginning of the surah. ﴿And a group of those with you﴾ is conjoined to the pronoun in taqum (you stand), and this conjunction was permitted without an emphatic word separating them. The standing in prayer of a group of his Companions was likewise, to emulate him. Among them were those who did not know how much of the night they had prayed and how much of it remained, so they would stand the whole night out of caution. They stood until their feet swelled, for a year or more, so it was lightened for them. ﴿And God measures﴾ (yuhsi, "counts") ﴿the night and the day. He knows that﴾ (an, here a lightened form of the heavy particle, its noun omitted, meaning "that He") ﴿you will not be able to count it﴾, i.e., the night, so that you would stand for what must be stood for, except by standing for all of it, and that would be hard on you. ﴿So He turned to you﴾ (raja'a bikum, "returned to you") ﴿with leniency﴾. ﴿So recite what is easy of the Qur'an﴾ in the prayer, by praying what is easy [for you]. ﴿He knows that﴾ (a lightened form of the heavy particle, i.e., "that He") ﴿there will be among you those who are sick, and others who travel in the land﴾ (yusafiruna, "journey") ﴿seeking of God's bounty﴾ (yatlubuna min rizqihi bi-l-tijara wa ghayriha, "seeking of His provision through trade and otherwise") ﴿and others who fight in the way of God﴾. Each of the three groups would find hard what was mentioned regarding standing in the night, so it was lightened for them by standing for what is easy of it. Then that was abrogated (naskh) by the five daily prayers. ﴿So recite what is easy of it﴾ as mentioned before. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾ (the obligatory one), ﴿and give the zakat, and lend to God﴾ by spending what is beyond the obligatory wealth in the way of goodness ﴿a goodly loan﴾, from a willing heart. ﴿Whatever good you send forward for yourselves, you will find it with God, better﴾ (khayran, "better") than what you left behind; it is a distinct [predicate], and what follows it, though not definite, resembles a definite because it is not declined for definiteness ﴿and greater in reward. And seek forgiveness of God; indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ to the believers.
